economy.summary: His campaign centers on affordability, saying he will address rising utility bills, housing costs, and concerns over where taxpayer dollars are going, with a pledge of transparency and accountability in the legislative process.
economy.short: Focuses on utility bills, housing costs, taxpayer-dollar accountability.

taxes.summary: His housing platform includes tackling high property taxes and promoting affordable homeownership; he has not published a broader tax or budget plan.
taxes.short: Proposes tackling high property taxes, promoting affordable homeownership.

education.summary: Advocates for full and equitable funding of the district's public schools and promotes comprehensive history instruction.
education.short: Advocates full, equitable public school funding; comprehensive history instruction.

healthcare.summary: Supports expanding Medicaid coverage and lowering prescription drug costs.
healthcare.short: Supports expanding Medicaid, lowering prescription drug costs.

energy.summary: Prioritizes access to safe drinking water and supports a transition to clean energy while preserving existing jobs.
energy.short: Prioritizes safe drinking water; clean-energy transition preserving existing jobs.

guns.summary: His public-safety platform supports enhanced training and resources for first responders and investment in violence prevention programs; it does not detail a position on gun laws.
guns.short: Supports first-responder resources and violence prevention programs.

economy.summary: Co-championed Senate Bill 6, a permitting-reform measure setting timelines for state agencies to review permit applications, saying that when permitting is unpredictable so is investment and that the bill signals Pennsylvania is open for business.
economy.short: Co-championed permitting-reform bill setting agency review timelines.

taxes.summary: Her campaign says she has supported only fiscally responsible state budgets that do not raise taxes, and that she posts all of her Senate office expenditures online for taxpayer review.
taxes.short: Says she supported only budgets that do not raise taxes.

abortion.summary: Voted for and co-sponsored a proposed state constitutional amendment declaring no constitutional right to abortion (SB 106, 2022), voted for a 2017 bill restricting abortions after 20 weeks, and called the Dobbs ruling a massive win for the rights of the unborn.
abortion.short: Voted for abortion restrictions; called Dobbs ruling a win.

education.summary: Her campaign says she wrote the law that allowed students to learn from home when schools were ordered to shut down during the pandemic.
education.short: Says she wrote pandemic-era law allowing learning from home.

healthcare.summary: Authored Act 146 of 2022, which sets standards and response deadlines for insurers' prior-authorization approvals of medical treatments, calling it one of the most significant health care reforms in the state in decades; her campaign also opposes state-mandated COVID-19 vaccination requirements.
healthcare.short: Authored prior-authorization reform law; opposes state vaccine mandates.

energy.summary: Says the most effective way to combat rising energy costs is to unleash the state's energy potential; supported a constitutional amendment opposing the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative and proposes legislation making it easier to switch electric and natural gas suppliers.
energy.short: Opposes RGGI; supports expanding state energy production, easier supplier switching.

guns.summary: Says she will not back down from defending the constitutional right of law-abiding citizens to bear arms, in a statement published with her 2022 endorsement by Gun Owners of America.
guns.short: Says she will defend law-abiding citizens' right to bear arms.
